title: Gaming in 2026: Marvel's Wolverine and GTA VI Face Fan Backlash | Entertainment
text:
In 2026, Marvel's Wolverine and Grand Theft Auto VI spark intense fan controversy amid a year of anniversaries, new releases, and industry challenges.
In 2026, the video game industry is experiencing a year of highs and lows. Celebrations for Resident Evil's 30th and The Legend of Zelda's 40th anniversaries, along with new releases like Pragmata and Mina the Hollower, have made the race for Game of the Year tighter than usual. However, controversy has also reached an all-time high, with Marvel's Wolverine and Grand Theft Auto VI facing intense scrutiny from fans.
The State of Gaming in 2026
2026 has been one of the greatest years for media in a long time, and video games in particular have had a better year than most. Resident Evil and The Legend of Zelda are both celebrating their 30th and 40th anniversaries respectively, with the former having a new movie and game and the latter releasing a remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, one of the best titles of all time, later in the year.
More than that, there are plenty of well-reviewed games such as Pragmata and Mina the Hollower, all of which are making the race for the 2026 Game of the Year even tighter than usual. However, it would not be a year of gaming if there was not plenty of controversy.
For as many good things that have happened in the game industry, there are as many bad things, from rising prices of games and consoles, more layoffs, and PlayStation's announcement that they will not support physical media in the future. However, the bad is expanding beyond the industry and finding itself in the culture of the fans.
Gamers are more critical than most fans in other mediums, but it has reached an all-time high in 2026. Two video games specifically have received the brunt of the hate this year, which includes Marvel's Wolverine and Grand Theft Auto VI. One of them is not even out yet, but both have been scrutinized by the community, making them the most controversial offerings of the year.
What Are Marvel's Wolverine and GTA VI About?
Before this list delves into the criticisms of fans and analyzes their reaction to these titles, it will first go through and detail what they are about. Marvel's Wolverine is Insomniac Games' most recent title, following their success with the Marvel's Spider-Man franchise to deliver another superhero game.
Announced in 2021, it took five years for this game to come out, and the reaction is mixed. This action-adventure game follows the titular hero, played by Liam McIntyre, as he gets involved with Team X after losing his memories. While he likes to do things himself, he finds new bonds with a group of mutants as they team up to fight the injustices against them. The combat is visceral, fast-paced, and absolutely engrossing, giving gamers the authentic Wolverine experience as they embody this role.
Next is Grand Theft Auto VI, which is hard to explain mainly because the game is not out yet, so no one knows its narrative. However, the game is set in Vice City and follows a Bonnie and Clyde-type relationship between Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, the voice actors of which have not been officially announced.
It has been over a decade since Grand Theft Auto V and eight years since Rockstar's last game, Red Dead Redemption 2, meaning this one is highly anticipated. While we do not know the main story, fans at least know what to expect in terms of gameplay, including a highly dense city to explore, captivating gunplay combat, detailed mini-games and random things to do, and hyperrealistic graphics.
The Discourse Surrounding These Games
Marvel's Wolverine is a good, but not great, video game, and Grand Theft Auto VI is not even out yet, but is likely to be the biggest video game of 2026. So, what exactly is the controversy surrounding them? Well, one common aspect is that they were highly anticipated, and now that Marvel's Wolverine has not lived up to expectations, fans are becoming extra critical.
Insomniac Games has a good track record, but Marvel's Wolverine is their lowest-rated video game and PlayStation's lowest-rated title in a while. Some of their titles were the best video games of the 2010s, but their most recent game has underwhelmed. What exactly is responsible for these low ratings?
Marvel's Wolverine features great combat that naturally lets the player learn the combos, but there are plenty of criticisms. The narrative is hard to critique since it is so subjective, with some fans loving the change of origin, and others hating the revamped differences.
The biggest criticism is the guidance, which holds the players' hand throughout the entire game. There are scent trails that directly lead the player to where they need to go, which seems redundant and over-the-top for a linear game. The characters also constantly tell the players what to do, and the collectibles have bright icons to notify players.
Meanwhile, as the most hyped video game potentially of all time, Grand Theft Auto VI has higher expectations than most, and that leads to more pressure. The trailers and extensive looks are spectacular for the most part, but fans have nitpicked anything they can find.
From awkward animations to reaching into a fridge and grabbing an invisible beer, gamers are overanalyzing everything about Grand Theft Auto VI. Other criticisms include the game being too woke, like Jason not being masculine enough. Outside the actual game, there is controversy surrounding the pricing and the fact that there is not a physical disc.
